citations.assessment: Ezra names Yehoshua among the priests and identifies him as son of Yotzadak. The verse does not supply the reported Ben Sira genealogy.
Haggai explicitly calls Yehoshua son of Yehotzadak high priest. The verse does not attest his descent to Ben Sira.
The opening confirms the tradition in a variant form, naming Ben Sira as grandson of Yehoshua. Preserve Heilprin’s report of a son and flag the divergence.
Heilprin quotes the possibility from a different case. The Bavli introduces it as a possibility, not as a report of an actual conception or a Ben Sira genealogy.
The pinned R. Zeira entry discusses the bath conception question directly.
The language in the Tartu OCR identifies Shalshelet HaKabbalah. Retain the foliation supplied by Heilprin; the printed folio in his specific edition remains uncollated.

evidence.witness: University of Tartu digitization, searchable Hebrew OCR

citations.assessment: Part I repeats the purported Maharil genealogy, without supplying a directly collated copy of Maharil.
Part I discusses the differing chronological opinions, reports the Yehoshua relationship as grandfather, and qualifies the account of grandson and publication.

holds.reason: Part I repeats this attributed statement. The exact Likkutei Maharil witness still needs collation.
Part I cites Tzemach David nearby, which warrants checking that work. The exact quoted rejection and the abbreviation remain unverified.
More than one Ben Sira work or introduction could be intended. Keep the specific printed work and locus open.
Shalshelet HaKabbalah supplies a generic Ketubot attribution; Heilprin records that he did not find it. No exact Ketubot locus admitted.
